title: Dedicated fleet autoscaler: burst controls, throughput guarantees, and utilization reporting
author: Priya Shah
description: Background: Dedicated fleets previously lacked fine-grained burst controls and per-fleet throughput guarantees. Operators asked for predictable SLAs for committed capacity while allowing safe, rate-limited bursts for short-term spikes. This PR implements a unified autoscaler policy that adds burst tokens, per-fleet throughput guarantees, and improved utilization reporting to inform both autoscaling and billing. What this PR does: Adds a burst-control token bucket to the fleet autoscaler, supports a configurable throughput_guarantee (tokens/sec) for dedicated pools, surfaces per-fleet utilization and burst consumption metrics to the telemetry pipeline, and introduces a safe migration path for existing fleets. The change is implemented end-to-end: control-plane config, autoscaler behavior, runtime admission checks, and observability. Design notes: - Burst control uses a token-bucket per-fleet counter with configurable capacity and refill_rate. Bursts can be consumed only when queueing latency is within SLO thresholds to avoid amplifying overloads. - Throughput guarantees reserve a baseline number of tokens / GPU-second for reserved capacity; autoscaler ensures target throughput by scaling to meet committed throughput before allowing bursts. - Utilization reporting: new telemetry keys (fleet.utilization_pct, fleet.burst_consumed, fleet.commitment_usage) are emitted at 1m granularity. These feed the Dedicated Console and billing reports. - Backwards compatibility: fleets without new config default to previous behavior (no burst tokens, autoscaler targets based on existing target_utilization). Migration is handled via a one-line fleet config update. Testing: Unit tests for token-bucket math and admission gating; integration tests covering scale-up/scale-down with bursts enabled; e2e canary on a trimmed dedicated cluster. Load tests show 18% improvement in spike-handling without impacting steady-state latency. Safety and rollout: Feature-gated under "dedicated_autoscaler_v2" remote flag. Rollout plan: enable for internal dedicated staging, monitor utilization and error rates for 48h, then enable for a small subset (5%) of customer fleets, followed by gradual increase. Automatic fallback to conservative autoscaling if error budget is breached. Checklist: - [x] Add autoscaler policy implementation (+ unit tests) - [x] Add runtime admission checks - [x] Emit telemetry metrics and dashboard updates - [x] Migration/messaging for fleets - [x] Docs and release notes - [x] Integration + e2e tests References: Linear ENG-1423 (autoscaler redesign), ENG-1588 (telemetry for dedicated), related PRs: pr-21437, pr-32148 for earlier burst control experiments.

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Overall this looks good. Two concerns: 1) token-bucket counter precision under high concurrency, 2) does throughput_guarantee interact with existing reserved_capacity math? Please add stress tests.

Priya Shah (author): Added high-concurrency stress test and addressed precision by switching from float64 to fixed-point micros. Updated autoscaler math to subtract reserved throughput before allowing bursts.
Ava Chen: Telemetry keys look good. Please ensure cardinality is bounded for fleet-level metrics.
Priya Shah: Telemetry emits only fleet-level aggregates (no per-node tags). Added doc note and dashboard that aggregates at fleet granularity to keep cardinality low.
Samir Patel: Can we detect and auto-disable bursts if observed tail latency increases by >20%? Suggest a circuit-breaker.
Priya Shah: Implemented an automatic fallback that disables burst consumption for 5m if p99 latency delta > 20% and emits an event. Added a test to simulate the condition.
ci_checks: integration-tests: initially failed (race in token_bucket), rerun: pass
merge_info: merge_notes: Feature gated behind dedicated_autoscaler_v2 flag. Post-merge: follow rollout checklist and watch dedicated.autoscaler.errors and fleet.utilization_pct dashboards for 48h.
release_notes: Added burst-control token-bucket and throughput guarantees for Dedicated fleets. Operators can configure burst_capacity and throughput_guarantee per-fleet; metrics (fleet.utilization_pct, fleet.burst_consumed) available in the Dedicated Console. Backwards compatible: old fleets keep previous behavior. Rollout gated under feature flag.
notes_for_ops: Enable remote flag 'dedicated_autoscaler_v2' for staging first. Watch p99_latency, fleet.utilization_pct, and fleet.burst_consumed. If tail latency regresses >20%, the autoscaler will automatically suspend bursts; manual rollback available via feature-flag toggle.
user_migration_instructions: To opt a fleet into burst controls add the following to fleet config: 'autoscaler: { policy: v2, burst: { capacity: 1000, refill_rate: 200 }, throughput_guarantee: 50 }'. See docs/dedicated/migration.md for examples and guidance.
